item.title: SCP-5925:
item.content:encoded:
This was a lot better then I thought it was going to be looking at the general premise- the idea of 'Blank is actually anomalous', or 'blank is actually an SCP', is boring and has been done so many times.

I'm pleased that this didn't fall into that, and I'm always happy to see more from 4000.

item.title: SCP-5129:
item.content:encoded:
A small complaint, but the picture should be near the top. And it should be formatted in such a way so you can see a caption below it.

This is entirely untrue. It can be wherever the author wants it to be placed and sometimes they don't want to have a caption. Other times they do.

Also, that's pretty clearly computer art. The picture should look as real as possible.

This is also pretty untrue. Many people use "computer art" and it turns out fine. Again its just kind of up to the author.

it would be cool if you could make a cool picture along with your SCP you don't have to find.

I'm a bit confused on what this means. And either way, you're still a little wrong with this.

We appreciate your willingness to help, but stick around a little and see whats up with the site first ;) Learning is one of the first steps to helping!

item.title: SCP-5925:
item.content:encoded:
I really enjoy this premise — I started to figure it out just before that telling crosslink, eliciting an "Aha!" from me, which is certainly a good sign. However, this piece is really quite rough around the edges. The sections written in blue appear to describe the desired version of the anomaly associated with its designation, but I got the sense that the anomaly's form is dependent on its own perception of its current name's connotations. Aside from the mechanics of the anomaly itself, I feel like the description and conprocs could have been more fleshed out and served as more of a hook for the article, as basically my only incentive to continue reading (prior to the addenda) was to see how it was connected to the region which shall remain unnamed. I'm also not really a fan of "access granted" being formatted as all lowercase, nor a single footnote that says "holly" as opposed to "Commonly known as holly" or something of that sort.

Clever, but unpolished. Novote.

EDIT: Will check back to see if my crit is implemented. Would be happy to upvote if so, because I really really enjoy this idea.

item.title: SCP-5295: Re: Staff Post - Deletion Vote
SCP-5295:
item.content:encoded: Is this an intentional homage to the butt ghost? If it is, I can kind of admire the attempt to make a joke article into a serious one, but I don't think you handled the execution very well. To me, at least, reading this felt like I was not in on some sort of reference — I don't really understand why you chose to include some details. I mean, fine, it's kind of weird for someone to have six whole chickens in their refrigerator, but I don't see the significance of that as it relates to the narrative. I'm also not sure why the wife would drown herself. -1.

item.title: SCP-5304:
item.content:encoded: I am not be an experienced writer, so maybe my opinion is not the best. But I think that the foundation pretending to be a fiction website, just like it is for us irl, building a link between truth and fiction is a great idea, but that I initially thought it was too great to work. I'm saying that this is a premise that I expected to fail absolutely or even sound somewhat cringe, and I bet many people thought about something like this but came out too weird, but your article came out great. I loved the way it was written, the way that chat logs were built and how it looks so real. I really enjoyed, thanks for the author for this :D

item.title: SCP-5133:
item.content:encoded:
Adding onto this, it feels more like a Series 1 SCP, which doesn’t mean it can’t be interesting, it just doesn’t really hold up to the standards we have today. Also there are some issues with the clinical tone. I would look into this and double check any future SCPs you make.
For example:

SCP-5133 is a Class B cognitive hazard but only affects the thalamus.

This should be changed to be:
“SCP-5133 is a Class B cognitive hazard, however it only affects the thalamus.”

item.title: Foundation Cool Achievement Badges:

… and non INT stuff:

Hey, I know that one! – Write an article about a minor Groups of Interest or person who has received little attention for some time or has no tag now.

Just a second. They did what?! – Write three articles about a situation where two groups or people who would otherwise never work together do just that. Bonus points the crazier it is. Minus points if they do it under a trick like brainwashing or unknowingly.
